title: [PDF] Tealbook B, September 2019 - Federal Reserve Board
summary: This Federal Reserve staff document, prepared for the September 18, 2019 FOMC meeting, presents three alternative policy statements (Alternatives A, B, and C) representing different options for the near-term path of monetary policy. Alternative B proposes a 25 basis point cut to bring the target range from 2-2.25% to 2-2%, Alternative A proposes a larger 50 basis point cut citing persistently below-target inflation, and Alternative C favors leaving rates unchanged at 2-2.25%. All three alternatives share identical assessments of current economic conditions, describing the labor market as strong, economic activity as rising moderately, and inflation as running below 2 percent.
key_points: Three policy alternatives were presented for the September 18, 2019 FOMC meeting: A (50bps cut), B (25bps cut), C (no change)
Under Alternative B, the target range for the federal funds rate would be lowered by ¼ percentage point to 2-2¼ percent
All three alternatives use identical language describing incoming data: solid job gains, low unemployment, moderate growth, soft business fixed investment and exports
All three alternatives note that overall inflation and core inflation are running below 2 percent
Alternative A asserts that market-based measures of inflation compensation have 'declined' (vs. 'remain low' in B and C), supporting a more aggressive 50bps cut
Alternative A removes 'contemplates' language and signals greater openness to additional rate reductions by stating the Committee will 'closely monitor' incoming data
The document references the July 2019 FOMC meeting where the target range was lowered to 2-2¼ percent, citing global developments and muted inflation pressures
why_it_matters: This Tealbook B document reveals the internal policy debate at the Federal Reserve ahead of the September 18, 2019 FOMC meeting. It shows that Fed staff was presenting a range of options from no action to a 50bps cut, demonstrating the genuine uncertainty and deliberation within the committee. The document also clarifies the significance of key phrasing like 'contemplates' versus 'closely monitors' in signaling the likely future path of policy. Market participants would have used this information to gauge the probability of different policy outcomes. Note: The September 18, 2019 meeting ultimately resulted in a 25bps cut (aligned with Alternative B).
macro_context: This September 2019 Tealbook was prepared at a time when global economic developments and below-target inflation were weighing on the Fed's policy outlook. The document shows the Fed was actively contemplating further accommodation, having already cut rates by 25bps in July 2019. The alternatives reflect genuine uncertainty about whether a modest additional cut (25bps) was sufficient or whether a more aggressive response (50bps) was warranted given persistent disinflationary pressures. This document predates the actual September 18 meeting decision.
market_structure_context: As a pre-FOMC meeting document, this Tealbook B would have been available to committee members in advance of the meeting. The range of options presented (no cut, 25bps, 50bps) indicates the genuine uncertainty facing policymakers. Market participants tracking Fed communications would analyze such documents to assess the probability distribution of potential outcomes.
important_numbers: 2-2¼ percent: target range under Alternative B
2-2½ percent: target range under Alternative A (50bps cut)
¼ percentage point: size of proposed cut under Alternative B
½ percentage point: size of proposed cut under Alternative A
2 percent: symmetric inflation objective referenced in all alternatives

issues_found: event_type 'fomc_statement' is incorrect: This is a staff preparation document (Tealbook B) presenting policy alternatives for FOMC members before a meeting. It is NOT an FOMC statement. The actual statement from the September 18, 2019 meeting would be a separate document. Proper event_type should be 'research_paper' or 'monetary_policy_report'.
source body was truncated due to character limits, potentially omitting additional pages with economic projections or detailed policy analysis from later sections of the document.

The summary references 'Alternative B proposes a 25 basis point cut to bring the target range to 2-2.25%' which is accurate for the document but note that the July 2019 statement (referenced in the document) already lowered rates to 2-2.25%. Alternative B would lower to 2-2%, not 2-2.25%. This creates minor ambiguity.
Historical document (2019) - approximately 6.5 years old - though still acceptable for archival value per protocol.
